title: Looking for a few game experts to join our Workbench pilot
author: Semantic_meaning
selftext:
The explosion in impressive game demos lately has been exciting to say the least...but if you're a talented game dev it also has to be quite unnerving to see things that would've taken months of planning, design, art, and dev get created in a weekend.

While it's amazing watching all of this unfold.. the expertise behind great game design feels a bit lost at the moment. Especially how to monetize it.

What seems to be omitted is that most of these impressive game demos (that are real) aren't coming from someone that just asked chatgpt to whip it up. They are coming from people that have enough expertise between game dev and efficient agent use to get these results. And a lot of it comes down to their setup (harness choice, model choice, skills, etc).

So, we've built an open standard for packaging that setup so that other devs can get some of those benefits: instructions, tools, environment, model choice, and a check that runs the game. We call it a workbench.  On one Godot task, we tested the same model/harness, one vanilla and one using a workbench, and the vanilla setup only shipped 1 working build out of 5 while the workbench one shipped 4 out of 5. 

This is early and we are a small team but the goal is crystal clear: give expertise a better way to be packaged, consumed, and commercialized. 

We're looking for a few game devs (ai only is fine) to build the first workbenches with us and earn ($$$) from their use. You're a fit if agents get your engine or pipeline subtly wrong without you, and you can define "working" in a way a script can check.

Comment or DM me. Full essay on the above in the comments.

Feel free to kick the tires yourself using the skill directly 

    npx skills add pompeii-labs/workbenches

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: Imma be honest, I have never seen ai make something impressive in a weekend. The impressive ai built demos just take months instead of years.

replies.author: Semantic_meaning
replies.body: We created a pirate themed multiplayer battle royale in a weekend. I get the bar for being impressed is rising, but this was incredibly impressive to me.

replies.author: JDad67
replies.body: I am working on a cozy pirate / sailing game. But single player only I think.

replies.author: Semantic_meaning
replies.body: such an awesome genre. what are you calling it?

replies.author: JDad67
replies.body: I don't know yet. But the progress Opus 5.5 made in 24 hours is blowing my mind.

replies.author: Blake9712
replies.body: I’m sure you made impressive progress but I highly doubt you made a fun game real people would want to play and spend money on in a weekend. All of the best ai projects I’ve seen have taken somewhere around 6 to 8 months and they’re demos. It only takes a little bit to get the concept of the idea going but it’s always so shallow in practice

comments.author: SnuffleBag
comments.body:
>The explosion in impressive game demos lately has been exciting to say the least...but if you're a talented game dev it also has to be quite unnerving to see things that would've taken months of planning, design, art, and dev get created in a weekend.

I stopped reading here. This is not a thing. There's not been a single impressive game demo or "thing that would've taken months" gotten created in a weekend. All of these "Opus 5.5 is amazing" posts are rubbish once you look past the initial 2 seconds novelty.

comments.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
comments.body: I've been working on talking pixels for 3 years, I'm licensed and verified to distribute keys and sell assets/games. I've been looking for a few people to help the daily run but I am not a $$$ first dev studio. My focus is to bring as much money to the creator/team as possible while being able to keep the lights on and belly fed. Currently I charge nothing, so if money is the motive for yall then it's probaly not for you.

comments.author: DOFFY292
comments.body: I think I might be the kind of person you’re looking for. I created this game [**https://store.steampowered.com/app/5284030/Soft\_17/**](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5284030/Soft_17/) in less than a month, without any prior game development skills. I invite you to try it out and get back to me if you’d like me to share my workflow with you.

replies.author: Semantic_meaning
replies.body:
Yeah this looks great! Congrats! Yes this is the type of work where I imagine you have learned a lot about what delivers better results than just asking vanilla claude for something. 

The idea is you can package your setup for a specific part of your build process, let's say you did a lot of refinement in getting claude (or whatever agent/harness you used) to create the aesthetics of cards in a certain way. You could package that, add it as a workbench, and then other devs can pull that down and get those results in their harness.
